reason: The text fragment consists of narratives describing the plagues of Egypt (frogs, flies, boils, hail, locusts, darkness) with Moses mediating between Pharaoh and Yahweh. While the passage extensively documents God's instructions and the plagues' devastating effects on Egypt and Egyptians, it contains no instances of the Hebrew people expressing blame toward their leaders (Moses/Aaron) or toward Yahweh. In fact, the Israelites are portrayed as protected (receiving light during the darkness plague: 'וּֽלְכָל־ בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָ֥יָה א֖וֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָֽם'). The people at risk are the Egyptians, not the Hebrew people. No complaint or accusation from the Israelites appears in the text.
